newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building union, employers agree wage deal.
newsitem.headline: German building union, employers agree wage deal.

text.p: Germany's construction sector union IG Bau and employers said on Friday they had agreed a wage deal, averting the threat of strike action in the troubled sector.
The new agreement enshrines higher sick pay than a previous deal rejected by the union's wages commission last Monday.
It cuts pay for the first three days of sickness to 80 percent of full year whereas the earlier agreement had cut sick pay for the first three weeks of illness.

In return, holiday bonuses will be reduced to 25 percent of monthly pay from 30 percent. Both employers' federations have already agreed to the pact. IG Bau's wages commission will decide later on Friday whether to approve the deal.
"The agreement stabilises incomes and gives companies certainty for their planning," Christian Democrat politician Heiner Geissler, who had moderated the talks, told a news conference.
Talks had resumed after the union's wages commission on Monday rejected a proposed deal reached in arbitration talks last week.
That deal offered a 1.3 percent pay rise from April 1 -- below the rate of German inflation -- a 20 percent cut in sick pay for the first three weeks of illness, and a cut in Christmas bonus.
The sick pay cut had been the main bone of contention.
